primary_metric: external process wall including suite preparation, tests, final cleanup, process startup/exit and result output
scope: one host, TCP, 48 isolated cases, Fresh/Fork, parallel1/4/8, 3 fresh processes per cell, no tail removal
correctness: 36 primary +12 warmup +4 positive pilot processes PASS; 4 wrong-seed negative processes fail and clean up as expected
conclusion: Fresh is shorter for mariamem in this workload. Fork acceleration is much larger for pgmem. Parallel startup and cleanup costs account for much of the P4 difference; long SQL spans affect P8 completion.
recommendation: Keep #88 as startup-cost probe. Record retirement/WaitDisconnected as an additional host-side candidate. #84 prewarming still requires a separate bounded overlap comparison.
limitations: No guest-internal cause attribution, Linux replication, general engine speed or semantic-parity claim.
Critical worker lanes reconstruct observed elapsed time; they are not CPU attribution or a causal speedup prediction.
pgmem r1 fork/P4 has586.7ms outside the internal suite timer; retained in external totals, cause unmeasured.
RSS is process lifetime high-water mark, not sampled batch peak or retained-child increment.
Two setup preflight failures occurred before any pilot, caused by directory/binary path collision and identity-reader path mismatch. No measured trial was discarded.
